 **Some things YOU can DO on Election Day…**

Be the First Voter – Represent John Q Public!

The First Voter in line at Poll Opening gets a special little ceremony where the leader (Inspector) of the Poll location tells him or her, “You represent THE PUBLIC. Your participation helps us preserve history and protect democracy”… Then they are shown the empty vote containers and zeroed out vote counters on machines before locking all of the bins! It would be AWESOME to have ANONS be that John Q. Public wherever possible this midterm elections!!

  • The Polling and Vote Tallying Procedures ARE PUBLIC! Bystanders are permitted to watch, but cannot interfere.
  • You CAN stay and watch the Poll Closing procedures!
  • Watch at the locations that have DAY-OF registration!
  • Look up and know your local voting rules. They will be on your REGISTRAR OF VOTERS website.

Some Interesting Polling Place Rules:

  • The Poll Workers will post signs that clearly say NO CAMPAIGNING of ANY kind after this point. Up to that zone, you can talk about candidates and ballot measures. No leaving election materials of any kind in booths.
  • Poll Watchers can ask about voting within 25 feet of the Polling Place.
  • A person may receive assistance if he “affirms” by making a statement that he is unable to mark his ballot. Any ballots helped by a worker have to be signed and logged as being helped.
  • Our County has a legal obligation to make Spanish language assistance and materials available to the voters. Other languages may be present in certain areas as well.
  • “Election corruption and/or intimidation include every person who threatens to make use of force or hires or arranges for any other person to make use of or threaten to make use of force/violence in order to compel a voter to refrain from voting or refrain from voting for a particular person or measure.”
  • “Every person who knowingly challenges a person’s right to vote without probable cause, or who engages in mass, indiscriminate, and groundless challenging of voters is punishable y imprisonment in the county jail or state prison."
  • To be eligible to vote at your polling place a voter must register to vote at least 15 days prior to Election Day. Voters who have missed the deadline vote by “Conditional Voter Registration process” where they go to the Election Divisions at their Government Center and complete a “Conditional Voter Registration” and get a PROVISIONAL BALLOT to vote.
  • The Ideal Voter is one who is 1) Registered, 2) Name and Address Match the precinct voter list. Provisional Ballots are given for those who do not fit those qualifiers for any reason, but no voter is turned away.
  • In California it is explicitly emphasized that we are NOT TO ASK FOR IDENTIFICATION.
  • Provisional Votes, Spoiled Ballots, surrendered Mail-In Ballots, are clearly marked, documented, and separated into secure bags. Voters are given a receipt and can track the status of their batch of votes.
  • NOTE: A PROVISIONAL BALLOT will REINSTATE a voter who has been noted as INACTIVE on the roster.

Poll Worker Procedures:

**BE A POLL WORKER IF YOU CAN IN THE FUTURE! ** In California the machines will all be new in 2020. Everyone will be a newbie. The people at the training were 20 years older than me! I’m NOT being ageist, but if you’re 18 or over, you can be a Poll Worker. Get involved! (Especially notice the Inspector duties! They are volunteers just like you or me, who may have volunteered as a clerk ONCE before.)

All duties are explicitly outlined and documented. Nothing is left to chance. Everyone has a step-by-step manual. I was amazed at how detailed the training program was, how step-by-step, and seemingly “idiot proof.” And yet, #eyeroll, people get ahead of procedures, and can’t work as teams, etc. When it is all said and done, they tried to build a better mousetrap, so to speak, and machines won’t work unless set up correctly, so whatever it takes for people to work together is what it takes.

Poll Inspector – Leader of a Poll Worker Team

  • Assigns duties (based on explicit directions).
  • RECEIVES MACHINE, PAPERWORK, AND ROSTERS THE NIGHT BEFORE, and prepares rosters by adding the late registered voters to the correct pages on the rosters.

Poll Workers – MAKE THE VOTING EXPERIENCE GREAT AGAIN!

  • Provide a safe and friendly voting experience (GOAL: NO CONFRONTATION)
  • Are given disability and voter sensitivity training & “NEVER turn a voter away!” Even unregistered voters are given options.
  • Can assist those who need it, but have to document who they assisted.
  • Helps people sign the Voter Roster, and cross references with another voter street index. (Voter Roster Street Index is a PUBLIC RECORD and is available for purchase by qualifying people or organizations.)
  • Helps people put their ballots through the counting machine after they are marked in the Polling Booth.
  • Give people their I VOTED STICKERS! =)
  • Help set-up and tear-down equipment, posters, etc. at the polling place.
  • There is a very clear and cross-referenced chain of custody for all equipment and ballots. Ballots are numbered in stacks of 50, so 50 Ballots will have THE SAME NUMBER to protect the secret ballot, but still make auditing possible. Every group of 500 Voted Ballots are carefully removed from the machine (it's full) contained, sealed, and documented.

AT CLOSE OF POLLS (Open to the Public)

  • Write-in and Auxiliary bags are counted before sealed, but regular ballots are sealed and certified.
  • A receipt from the machines is printed for an audit trail. A Statement of Votes cast is taped on the door at the polling place FOR THE PUBLIC. No copies of it are permitted, but you can write down the info.
  • PROVISIONAL VOTES are counted last, if necessary. Probably because there is a lot of verification that needs to happen. If a vote is closer than the number of Provisional Votes, then obviously that vote counting takes longer and they will be counted.
  • There is 1 month to finalize the vote count.
  • Inspector returns equipment and ballots to the Election Board, completing the chain of custody.
